title: Evidence-Gated Residual Representation (EGRR)
question: Can sensitivity-selected sparse residual corrections improve low-bit quality at matched serialized storage, compared with simpler selection rules?
reviewedBy: Claude (Anthropic, Opus 5.5), drafted at Chad Holland's direction; human review level: outcome review by Chad Holland (2026-10-22)

observations.text: Calibration MSE on one 16×8 synthetic case (seed 28, 3-bit quantizer, 8 corrections, 111 EGR2 bytes per corrected arm): covariance-greedy 0.8220074902, residual magnitude 0.8896527392.
observations.limitation: The same calibration inputs were used for selection and evaluation, so this is not held-out improvement or generalization. Raw arrays and run logs were not archived.

observations.text: 21 of 21 local structural and numerical tests reported passing at commit 2885adbc.
observations.limitation: Logs and exit codes were not archived; PA has not re-run them. A passing test is not a scientific result.

adverse.text: No useful lower support or variance bound has been proven for the population P1 ratio estimand, so the proposed fixed-sample 5% claim is unresolved and not approved.
The canonical aggregator accepted 100 constructed non-EGR2 stand-in records as valid; it trusts a reported decode flag instead of decoding the bytes.

openDecisions.text: Statistical estimand and decision rule for P1
Selector conventions, tolerances and control arms before any protocol freeze
A mandatory verification boundary: decode, reconstruct and rescore before aggregation; registration loaded by the entrypoint, not supplied by the caller
Delivery of the contributor's retained qualification package for inspection

nextReview: When the qualification package is delivered or fork PR #2 changes. No date is scheduled and nothing here authorizes a run.
